what: Chaitanya cult: post of Gosain/spiritual guide not confined to Brahmans, some are Baidyas; descended from Chaitanya's entourage. Vaishnava, not Daśanāmī.
quote: A peculiarity of Ohaitanya's cult is that the post of spiritual guide or Gosain is not confined to Brahmans, and several of those best known belong to the Baidya caste.

what: Jat Baishtams or Bairagi: casteless Chaitanya followers, recruits from all castes, form a community like an ordinary caste; reputation tarnished by recruits joining over love intrigues or caste expulsion.
quote: The latter, who are also known as Jat Baishtams or Bairagi, consist of recruits from all castes, who profess to intermarry freely among themselves

what: Rash Jatra at Santipur in Kartik: idols of the Gosains carried in procession; Santipur also a bathing place. Vaishnava Gosains.
quote: when the Rash Jatra festival lasts for two days and ends with a procession in which the idols of the Gosains are carried about on elevated wooden platforms.

what: Kartabhaja sect: founder Ram Saran Pal, helped by a Fakir (Fakir Thakur) who established a band of Fakirs; a syncretic sect, not Daśanāmī.
quote: With him was associated a religious mendicant who was known as Fakir Thakur.

what: Temple of Jugal Kishor with images of Krishna and Radha founded by first mahanth Ganga Ram Das, about 1728; Maharaja Krishna Chandra granted 125 bighas rent-free. Vaishnava temple.
quote: Ganga Ram Das, the first mahanth of the temple. ... who made a grant of 125 bighas of feut^free laad for the support of the temple.
